PullRequest.Title: eslint: forbid contrib/chat from importing contrib/sessions
PullRequest.Body:

Sessions depends on chat, never the reverse. Code under `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/**` must not import from `src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/**`. Until now nothing enforced this: `local/code-import-patterns` allows any `vs/workbench/contrib/*/~` import from a contribution. It checks layers, not which way contributions may depend on each other.

This PR makes such imports a lint **error**. The four files that violate it today are allowlisted until #346756 removes them, so no new violations can be added in the meantime.

### What changed

- **New local rule `local/code-no-restricted-path-imports`** (`.eslint-plugin-local/code-no-restricted-path-imports.ts`). It resolves each import specifier (relative paths and `vs/` aliases, normalized) to a repository path and reports it when it matches one of the `paths` globs in its options, using that entry's message.
  - **What it checks:** static imports, re-exports (`export … from` and `export *`), `import type`, inline `import('…')` types, `import x = require()`, and dynamic `import()` and `require()` calls whose argument is a string or a template literal without substitutions.
  - **`require()`:** only the global `require` is checked; a locally declared `require` is skipped.
  - **What it ignores:** node modules. Computed dynamic imports can't be resolved statically, so they aren't enforced; the README says so.
  - **Why resolve paths:** non-canonical specifiers such as `./../..//sessions/…` are caught, and `vs/sessions` or an unrelated folder named `sessions` is not flagged.
- **`eslint.config.js`:** a new block for `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/**/*.ts` turns the rule on as an error for `src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/**`. Today's violators are listed by exact path in its `ignores`, with a comment pointing to #346756; remove each entry once its import is gone:
  - `chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostCustomizationService.ts`
  - `chat/browser/chatTipCatalog.ts`
  - `chat/test/browser/chatTipService.test.ts`
  - `chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatToolAuthenticationSubPart.test.ts`
- **Tests:** `.eslint-plugin-local/tests/code-no-restricted-path-imports.test.ts` covers 11 import forms against forbidden sources (including non-canonical and absolute ones) and allowed sources (`vs/sessions`, a folder named `sessions` inside chat, `contrib/sessionChanges`, a node module). It also includes a locally declared `require`, a `require` parameter and a computed dynamic import.
- **Docs:** a README section for the rule.

### Why not an existing mechanism

- **`local/code-import-patterns`:** it uses the first target that matches, and its restrictions list what is *allowed*. Excluding `contrib/sessions` for chat would mean copying the whole contrib allow list, plus extra targets for the allowlisted files.
- **`no-restricted-imports` and its typescript-eslint version:** they match the raw specifier text, so they miss dynamic imports, `import()` types and non-canonical relative paths. They also flag `vs/sessions` and any folder named `sessions`. Reusing the base rule for chat files would also replace its existing `src/vs` options there.

No product code changes. `valid-layers-check` and hygiene need no changes: the layers check doesn't use eslint, and hygiene uses the same eslint config.

### Validation

- `node --test .eslint-plugin-local/tests/code-no-restricted-path-imports.test.ts`: passed (113/113). Against the earlier versions of the rule, the template-literal and shadowed-`require` cases failed.
- `node --test .eslint-plugin-local/tests/*.test.ts`: passed (613/613).
- `pnpm run eslint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat`: passed, 1545 files, 0 problems.
- With the allowlist temporarily removed, `npx eslint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat` reported exactly the 4 allowlisted files (5 imports).
- **Probe:** I temporarily added forbidden imports to non-allowlisted chat files: a static import, a `./../..//` path, an export-from, a dynamic `import()`, an inline `import()` type, a template-literal `import()`, and an `import type` in a test. `npx eslint` reported all 7 as `local/code-no-restricted-path-imports` errors. Reverted.
- `npx eslint eslint.config.js` and the new rule and test files: passed.
- `pnpm run typecheck` in `.eslint-plugin-local`: no new errors. It already fails on `main` with 21 listener-typing errors in existing rules, and the count is unchanged.
- The pre-commit hygiene hook passed.

An independent review on a different model returned SHIP after two fix rounds.

Refs #346756

Scenarios.Scenario: Developer or CI lints src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat, including the full-repository lint required when a local ESLint rule/configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ESLint loads the flat config and local plugin, reads/parses requested TypeScript files, then the new rule resolves and matches each supported import occurrence before lint results are available. The rule is on the lint critical path but never on the VS Code product runtime path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover and load local rule modules, including the newly added rule module.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional module load per ESLint worker/config process; the existing directory scan remains one readdirSync per process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The plugin index scanned the same directory and loaded every existing rule, but this rule module did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The extra module load is part of ESLint startup, but it is a single bounded file load and minimatch/path dependencies were already loaded by other local rules.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the source files selected for linting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For a targeted chat lint, up to the chat subtree's files; for the PR's plugin/config change, changedFiles selects the full repository. The new rule itself performs zero filesystem operations per import.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: ESLint already read and parsed the same selected source files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Source reads and parsing dominate the lint path and must complete before results; their cardinality is unchanged by the rule.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU work grows linearly with matching chat files and their AST/import and call-expression counts; glob matching grows with configured path entries, currently one. There is no collection-to-boundary multiplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The repository ESLint runner uses concurrency: 'auto', so files are distributed across ESLint workers. Within one file, AST listeners execute synchronously; the configured restriction list has one pattern and no asynchronous fan-out or queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The repository runner enables ESLint's content cache. A cold or configuration-invalidated run executes the new rule for matching chat files; warm unchanged files can be skipped by ESLint. The rule has no cross-file cache, but each import check is bounded to path normalization and one configured minimatch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: config scope, listeners, path resolution, matching, runner cache, and worker concurrency are directly visible in the changed and surrounding code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact added milliseconds depend on cache state, worker count, and import/call density. The work is simple, bounded, and lint-only, so there is no evidence of a material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff adds bounded linear CPU work to an intentional lint check, with no per-import I/O, network, IPC, subprocess, unbounded retention, or product-path impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build test suite runs the new RuleTester coverage
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The build test command loads the new test file and TypeScript parser, then RuleTester parses and lints the generated snippets before this test file completes. Other test files may run concurrently under node:test, while cases in this suite are bounded and in-memory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the added test and its imported rule/parser modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One added test-module load per build test invocation, plus normal dependency module loads shared through the Node module cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The build test glob did not find or load this test file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The test file must load before its cases run, but the boundary count is fixed and does not scale with repository contents.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Parser CPU/allocation follows the fixed Cartesian test data: 7 allowed sources by 11 forms, 5 restricted sources by 11 forms, three special cases, and three direct resolver tests. It does not scale with user data or repository size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: node --test schedules test files through its runner; this file defines a fixed matrix of RuleTester cases. No changed limiter, mutex, subprocess pool, or external-service concurrency is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no persistent result cache for these unit cases; Node's module cache coalesces repeated imports within the process. Every suite run intentionally executes the fixed cases.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the generated case counts and build test glob are explicit in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timing is provided, but snippets are tiny and the repository already uses similarly broad RuleTester matrices for import-rule coverage.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added test work is bounded, intentional validation rather than an accidental hot-path multiplier, and there is no evidence that it materially delays the build test stage.

Scenarios.Scenario: VS Code chat and sessions product runtime, including startup and chat interaction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: No changed file is bundled into or executed by the VS Code workbench. The ESLint config, local rule, and tests are development/build tooling, so product startup, rendering, input, chat requests, and sessions workflows have no new prerequisite work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: No user, session, message, repository, or UI collection reaches the changed code at runtime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No product-runtime tasks, queues, workers, or remote operations are introduced or changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No product cache keys, hit/miss behavior, invalidation, negative caching, or coalescing changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because every changed file is ESLint configuration/plugin documentation or tests and the rule is only enabled through eslint.config.js.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None for runtime reachability; the change is absent from the product execution path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Product performance is unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and surrounding ESLint plugin, runner, cache, test, and change-scope code. The only added costs are bounded lint-time AST/path checks, one rule-module load per ESLint process/worker, and fixed unit-test cases; no actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
